title: He said it at the foot of an execution.
paragraphs: He said it at the foot of an execution.

Not in a church.
Not during worship.
But staring at a broken, bleeding man on a cross.
“Surely… He was the Son of God.” — Mark 15:39
A Roman centurion. Hardened. Pagan. Trained to kill without flinching.
And yet—something shattered him.

Not the nails.
Not the blood.
Not even the darkness that covered the land.
It was how Jesus died.

No curses.
No revenge.
No desperation.
Only mercy.
“Father, forgive them…”
And in that moment, the soldier realized—this was no ordinary man. This was God in flesh, absorbing wrath he didn’t deserve… for people who did.
But here’s what we miss…
You don’t need to stand at Calvary to say those words.
Every time you see your sin clearly—your pride, your hidden battles, your quiet compromises—you are standing at the cross again.
And the question echoes:
Who do you say He is?

Just a teacher?
A prophet?
Or the Son of God… who died for you?
Because if He is the Son of God, then this changes everything.

Your sin is not the end of your story.
Your shame doesn’t get the final word.
Your past is not your identity.
Jesus didn’t just die to impress a soldier.
He died to save you.
And He didn’t stay in that tomb.
He rose—so you could rise too.
So today, don’t just admire the cross.
Surrender at it.
Say it not just with your lips—but with your life:
“Surely… You are the Son of God.”
